name: Why agencies run on Runnit
description: Four things studio owners get on day one.

features.name: Everything in one dashboard
features.commentary: Most studio owners start the day across five tabs and three spreadsheets. Runnit opens on a single dashboard showing overdue work, client workload mix and what your automations have been doing overnight.

features.name: Task triage that takes seconds
features.tagline: Overdue, due today, upcoming — already sorted
features.commentary: Tasks arrive pre-sorted into overdue, due today and upcoming, with tracked and remaining time on every row. You clear bottlenecks instead of hunting for them.

features.name: A week you can actually see
features.tagline: Spot the overloaded days before they bite
features.commentary: The schedule lays the week out by day and time, so an overloaded Tuesday is obvious at a glance rather than something you discover when a deadline slips.

features.name: Every project, every stage
features.tagline: One pipeline instead of a sheet per client
features.commentary: Projects sit in stage columns — planning, in progress, internal review, client review. One pipeline replaces the sheet-per-client sprawl, and it stays true as you scale.
